requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: The attribute is added to every generated formatter and resolver type (new test passes on head, fails on base), but every occurrence is wrapped in '#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK' on the false premise that the attribute does not exist there. It does exist in netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+, so consumers on those targets still get no exclusion, while the issue asks for all generated code to be decorated.

findings.title: Preprocessor guard excludes netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework based on a false premise
findings.claim: System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute ships in .NET Framework 4.0+ (System.dll) and in netstandard2.0 (netstandard.dll). I confirmed it in the reference assemblies on this machine and by compiling a netstandard2.0 project that uses it. The guard means consumers targeting netstandard2.0 or any .NET Framework, which includes many library and Unity-adjacent consumers, get no exclusion. The README and test comment state the false premise as fact, and the second new test locks the guard in.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the #if guard (the generator already requires a consumer that references MessagePack, which targets netstandard2.0+/net472+), and update README, the test comment and the guard test.

findings.title: Attribute on the generated half of user-declared partial resolvers can break builds (CS0579) and silently hides user code
findings.claim: The resolver and composite resolver templates emit '[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] partial class <ResolverName>' for a class the user declares as partial. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute has AllowMultiple = false. A user who already put [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on their partial resolver declaration will get error CS0579 'Duplicate attribute' after upgrading on the targets where the guard is active (I reproduced CS0579 with two partial declarations each carrying the attribute). Even without a conflict, the attribute applies to the whole type, so any hand-written members in the user's partial resolver are now excluded from coverage too.
findings.suggested_fix: On the user-declared partial resolver, put the attribute on the generated members (Instance field, GetFormatter method, nested FormatterCache/GetFormatterHelper classes) instead of the type, or skip it when the user's declaration already carries the attribute.

findings.title: Unrelated-looking whitespace change in TransformUtilities is required by the change but widens the snapshot churn
findings.claim: The brace emitted after a nesting type with constraints now ends with a newline. This is needed because a '#if' directive must start its own line, but it also changes generated output for nested generic types independently of the attribute. Covered by snapshot tests that pass.
